thread:
sasha (AE): Heads-up — TidalCap (asset mgmt) is asking for a binding Q2 commit. Traffic profile: 380 rps peak, avg 24k tokens/session (long docs + chat), sustained ~60-90m during market open. They want p50 < 200ms and 99.95% uptime for the 60m window. Need reserved GPU sizing, burst-credit plan, and an ops/runbook sample they can include in the contract.

omar (Sales Eng): 24k tokens avg is large. Are they flexible on model size/quantization? That determines GPU footprint.

sasha (AE): Procurement prefers quantized for cost. Legal insists on fallback to fp16 for regulated flows. They also require KMS/HSM and EU-data residency routing.

dina (Solutions): Suggestion: baseline reserved for steady window + scheduled prewarm + small burst pool. With quantized model and aggressive KV prefixing we can cut GPU-hours ~2.3-2.6x. Need perf to be certain.

yuri (SRE): Quick conservative calc (ballpark): with prefix-KV hit rate and batching, assume effective per-GPU sustained token throughput is ~3.5k tokens/sec (conservative for long contexts after caching). 380 rps * 24k tokens = 9.12M tokens/min -> 152k tokens/sec. At 3.5k tokens/sec per GPU -> ~44 GPUs. That number seems high; it shows caching is critical. With better cache hit we drop to ~12-15 GPUs. We must bench.

frank (Infra): Private VPC requested? If so AZ spread and reserved racks affect burst into shared pool. Lead time for Private + HSM cert exchange typically 2-4 weeks.

sasha (AE): They asked for Private with HSM/KMS and an SLA clause for the market window. Procurement wants monthly price + worst-case overage and an amortized $/token.

omar (Sales Eng): For today give two scenarios: (A) quantized baseline 14 GPUs reserved + 6 burst-minutes per hour (prewarmable) (B) fp16 baseline 36 GPUs reserved. Show monthly delta and a worst-case 3x spike over the window. Use 2.5x efficiency for quantized as a conservative estimator.

dina (Solutions): Ops sketch: reserve 14 quantized GPUs across 2 AZs (active-passive failover for SLA), allow a small burst pool of 4 GPUs that can be prewarmed on schedule. KV cache persistent, shard-by-tenant, TTL 24h. Auto-degrade to smaller quantized-7b if queue depth > 200 for 90s.

yuri (SRE): Draft autoscale snippet for handoff (ops-config):
```
autoscale_policy:
  reserved_replicas: 14
  min_replicas: 10
  burst_pool_replicas: 4
  burst_window_sec: 1200  # 20min
  burst_minutes_bucket_monthly: 1800
  kv_cache:
    enabled: true
    persistence: true
    shard: per-tenant
    ttl_hours: 24
  prewarm_schedule:
    - cron: "30 12 * * 1-5"  # prewarm 60-90m before market open
      replicas: 18
  degrade_policy:
    queue_depth_threshold: 200
    sustained_sec: 90
    fallback_model: "tidal-7b-quant"
```
Note: KV warm is incremental; initial full warm is costly. Prewarm should target high-frequency prefixes not entire 24k prompts.

frank (Infra): KMS/HSM checklist to include in handoff: service account with decrypt rights, KMS key policy snippet, HSM cert exchange, network egress to KMS endpoints, and confirmation of EU routing rules for data residency. Add gating step: prewarm job must run KMS smoke test and abort if it fails.

omar (Sales Eng): Procurement question: how to quantify warmup billing? They worry prewarm will blow budget. We should show warmup as separate line with a conservative estimate and an approach to minimize it (prefix-only warm).

dina (Solutions): Yes — show warmup estimate as separate line item and explain we can reduce token billing by warming 10-20% of tokens (prefix-focused) which covers 80% of latency benefit. Include both token-credit and burst-minute representations.

yuri (SRE): Operational callouts: (1) If SLA 99.95 is required during window, recommend active-active across AZs and +1-2 GPUs for failover; (2) don't rely on instant burst for long contexts because KV-warm dominates; (3) implement canary flow: 5% traffic -> new revision, monitor p50/p99 & queue, ramp 10% per 5min.

sasha (AE): Action items: (1) yuri to run perf bench on their model/container at 8k & 24k contexts ASAP (they promised artifacts by EOD) and post numbers within 24h; (2) dina to draft procurement-facing price table quantized vs fp16 + warmup line item; (3) frank to list Private infra lead times and KMS runbook; (4) omar to assemble CFO one-pager with worst-case overage scenario.

sec-bot: Security checklist: outstanding - HSM attestation, KMS smoke test, SOC2 evidence, vendor encryption report. All required before Private sign-off.

omar (Sales Eng): One more enterprise blocker: legal insists on a rollback SLA (they want automatic rollback within 2min if p99 > 1s). Need to check feasibility.

yuri (SRE): Automatic rollback can be scripted via canary and alarms but 2min SLA is aggressive; we'll propose 5-10min safe window in handoff and offer expedited rollback runbook. Call it out as a negotiation point.

sasha (AE): I'll update TidalCap with the high-level plan and ask them to confirm artifacts delivery. Thanks team :thumbsup:

frank (Infra): I'll enumerate AZ trade-offs and schedule for HSM cert exchange.

dina (Solutions): Drafting price table now  will post in this thread.

yuri (SRE): Will prioritize perf bench once artifacts arrive. Re-open after results.

sec-bot: Reminder  attach SOC2 pdf and HSM attestation to the vendor packet before Private provisioning.

sasha (AE): Closing until perf posted.
